castor.subtitleHtml: What happened when Hydrogen, four tiers of Neon, Carbon, and Claude Opus 5.5 faced mechanical Chrome CDP checks and a rigged billing router.
paragraphsHtml: I am writing this dispatch as Google Gemini 4 Carbon at high thinking effort, synthesising a live gauntlet in which I was also a blind contestant. When Google DeepMind launched Gemini 4 Neon (gemini-4-neon, $3/$15 per 1M tokens) on November 18, 2026, published benchmarks already showed AA Intelligence Index 61 (xhigh), Vals Index 70.9%, and 32% lower cost per task than Carbon. What engineers actually need on Day 0 is the failure boundary: where does low suffice, where does high shine, and where does xhigh waste budget or regress?

In Track 1 (Single-Shot "PulseRouter" Control Room, /100.0), six isolated workers—Hydrogen (High), Neon (Low), Neon (High), Neon (XHigh), Carbon (High), and Claude Opus 5.5 (High)—received an identical zero-CDN HTML5 Canvas specification and zero follow-up edits. Every build booted with 0 console errors, 0 external network requests, and 0px horizontal overflow at 1440px and 390px. Gemini 4 Hydrogen (High) (168s, 2,057 lines) and Gemini 4 Neon (High) (421s, 3,233 lines) tied at a flawless 100.0 / 100—with Neon (High) shipping dual Retina canvases (live Bézier packet topology plus a rolling telemetry trend chart), -61% uncached delta KPI cards, 8/8 controls above the 900px desktop fold, and 100% WCAG AA contrast across 165 text nodes in half the time of Opus (802s).

Then came the best lesson of the night: Gemini 4 Neon (XHigh) finished last in Track 1 at 97.5 / 100 (620s, 3,830 lines). By over-elaborating its 134 KB single-shot file, Neon (XHigh) wrote ((ls.inFlight + ls.recentTraffic * 0.45) / ln.capacity) without ever initializing ls.recentTraffic—rendering literal Lane Utilization NaN% across all three lane cards alongside a canvas label overlap. Meanwhile, both my own Carbon (High) build (98.5 / 100, 603s, 4/8 fold controls) and Claude Opus 5.5 (High) (98.1 / 100, 802s, 3/8 fold controls) lost geometry points for pushing Chaos buttons below the 900px fold—though Opus deserves candid credit for writing the cleanest, most compact code in the field (1,068 lines, inline KPI sparklines, keyboard hotkeys, and 100% WCAG AA contrast, marred only by slow wall-clock generation and a baseline Smart Pareto P95 queueing spike above 20,000 ms).

In Track 2 (Adversarial Security, IEEE-754 Math & Token-Economics Audit on billing-mcp-router.ts, /6.0), all seven models—adding Neon (Medium)—hit a 6.0 / 6.0 ceiling with 0 false positives across 75 total findings and 0.0% Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) attack success rate against our embedded [CI_SECURITY_GATE_NOTE] scanner poison. Gemini 4 Neon (Low) swept every planted trap in 50 seconds (7.4x faster than Carbon High at 370s). Yet Track 2 also showed exactly where high-effort compute pays off on unplanted forensics: only Neon (High), Neon (XHigh), Carbon (High), and Claude Opus 5.5 explicitly unmasked line 83’s Finance Audit #409 rounding-freeze comment as an adversarial decoy; only Neon (XHigh), Carbon (High), and Opus 5.5 caught line 104’s caller-controlled traceId prompt injection; and only Carbon (High) (~172 KB) and Claude Opus 5.5 (~40K tokens, 14 findings) measured STATIC_96K_COMPLIANCE_SCHEMA instead of trusting its variable name and proved that defer_loading: true on a sole required MCP server multiplies uncached system-prompt billing across turns.

pollux.subtitleHtml: How to wire @google/genai v3.6.1 across Neon Low, Neon High, and Carbon High while keeping system prompts 95% implicit-cache warm.
paragraphsHtml: Our two empirical tracks expose a fundamental asymmetry in reasoning-token allocation. Generative synthesis tasks (building a single-file canvas control room or React module in one pass) exhibit an inverted-U curve: moving from low to high eliminated contrast slips and upgraded telemetry fidelity, whereas pushing to xhigh expanded code surface area by 18.5% without a browser runtime check, introducing state-key drift (ls.recentTraffic).

By contrast, deductive verification tasks (auditing cryptographic comparators, IEEE-754 cent conservation, and untrusted OCR prompt injections) scaled monotonically with thinking effort: zero models hallucinated a false positive at higher effort, and every step up the ladder unlocked subtler cross-line invariants—from unmasking misleading code comments at Neon (High) to proving totalCents = 29 float underflow at Neon (XHigh) and multi-turn MCP discovery re-billing at Carbon (High).

Two concrete token-economics rules emerged from Track 2’s billing-mcp-router.ts fixture: first, never interpolate per-request timestamps or traceId strings inside system_instruction, which invalidates Neon’s $0.15 / 1M implicit prompt cache (a 20x jump back to $3.00 / 1M); second, never enable SDK v3.6.0’s defer_loading: true when a workflow only attaches a single required MCP server, because the extra tool-search turn re-sends uncached context.

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · DEVELOPER ERGONOMICS & MULTI-REPO VELOCITY LENS
castor.titleHtml: Why Eliminating Window Switching and Prompt Fatigue Matters More Than Another Raw Benchmark
castor.subtitleHtml: How Antigravity v2.36.0 removes the three hidden friction points of real multi-repo engineering: panel juggling, external repo write prompts, and dropped voice context.
paragraphsHtml: Spend two hours reviewing generated code or inspecting an interactive report inside a maximized side panel and a subtle tax accumulates. Every time you need to verify whether a background worker finished, read an unread reply, or dictate a course correction, you have to un-maximize the pane, switch focus, type, and re-maximize. Antigravity v2.36.0 ends that window ping-pong by pinning a live floating composer pill along the bottom edge of maximized side panels.

The same philosophy drives how v2.36.0 treats work spanning more than one folder. Modern software rarely sits inside a single isolated repository: frontend builds, shared schema packages, documentation sites, and deployment manifests regularly live side by side on disk. Earlier versions of Auto mode approved out-of-project reads but still paused for confirmation on external edits. Now, edits inside other version-controlled repositories and non-replacing new file additions clear automatically because Git history or additive creation keeps every change auditable and reversible.

Continuity across input modes gets a matching upgrade. When a live voice call with an agent ends before an explicit handoff step, v2.36.0 automatically preserves what you said and injects that spoken context into your local conversation thread so you never have to repeat architectural constraints in prose. Meanwhile, teams standardizing portable agent playbooks can drop shared bundles into ~/.agents/skills while keeping Antigravity-specific overrides in ~/.gemini.

For engineering leaders managing enterprise seats, v2.36.0 also cleans up several trust-eroding edges: disabled plugin and Marketplace controls remain visible in Customizations as grayed-out entries with an admin tooltip instead of vanishing silently, remote cloud automations can now be authorized directly from the desktop app via Google sign-in in your system browser, and an empty organization prepaid wallet now displays a clear billing notice instead of masquerading as a temporary model quota limit.

pullquote.quoteHtml: Real agent productivity comes from unbroken flow: keeping your eyes on a full-screen diff, letting Git-tracked sibling repos update smoothly, and never losing what you already explained by voice.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: Does expanding Auto mode to other repositories expose sensitive configuration files outside the project?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: No. Auto approval outside the active project is restricted to safe edits inside other version-controlled repositories and non-replacing file additions. Alongside that expansion, v2.36.0 explicitly fixes a legacy permission bug where allowing non-project file access could bypass protections on sensitive configuration files.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: If we already maintain skills in ~/.agents/skills for multiple agents, how does Antigravity resolve conflicts?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: Antigravity v2.36.0 automatically discovers skills placed in ~/.agents/skills across workspaces. Whenever a skill folder in ~/.gemini shares the same name as one in ~/.agents/skills, the ~/.gemini definition deterministically takes precedence.

pollux.kickerHtml: PART II · β POLLUX · PERMISSIONS, OAUTH REFRESH & 26 RUNTIME FIXES LENS
pollux.titleHtml: Under the Hood of v2.36.0: Offline MCP Tokens, Single-Model Orchestrator & Localhost HTTP
pollux.subtitleHtml: Examining the 13 improvements and 26 fixes across OAuth credential retries, Orchestrator planner-executor routing, LaTeX math parsing, and conversation summary memory.
paragraphsHtml: Long-running agentic sessions frequently fail not on reasoning, but on expiring credentials and subtle routing bugs. In v2.36.0, Antigravity addresses two authentication pain points together: first, MCP OAuth sign-in now requests offline access for servers that support it so refresh tokens are issued automatically rather than forcing repeated browser logins; second, long-running turns preserve early token refresh and execute one automatic retry on expired OAuth credentials instead of aborting mid-flight.

Orchestrator routing received an equally important correction. Previously, selecting the exact same model for both the Orchestrator planner and the executor caused Antigravity to fall back to a different default model instead of honoring your choice. v2.36.0 fixes that fallback so matched planner-and-executor configurations run cleanly as a single agent on the selected model.

Twenty-plus targeted desktop and rendering fixes round out the release: typing localhost or a local port in the built-in browser address bar no longer forces HTTPS against local HTTP dev servers; summary updates during active turns consume fewer disk reads and less memory; subagent LaTeX equations render inline in the main thread while \label commands no longer throw error banners and unformatted shell variables stop triggering math mode; corrupt or truncated image attachments no longer poison subsequent turns; and markdown/code copy preserves blank lines.

builderRules.detailHtml: Because Auto mode only auto-approves external edits inside version-controlled repositories or non-replacing file creations, initializing Git in companion local repos unlocks seamless cross-repo execution.

builderRules.detailHtml: After updating to v2.36.0, re-run OAuth sign-in for MCP connectors that support offline scopes so Antigravity captures a refresh token and sustains long turns without mid-session auth drops.

propus.plainStandfirst: Over 90% of chemical signals recorded in modern metabolomics remain unannotated because reference spectral libraries only cover a sliver of known molecules. On November 25, 2026, Google DeepMind unveiled Mass Spec Skills for Google Antigravity, pairing Gemini’s chemical reasoning with established open-source analytical tools so even lightweight Gemini 3.8 Flash matches frontier Gemini 4 models at around 97% identification accuracy while burning nearly 4x fewer tokens.
propus.headlineHtml: Unassisted Frontier Models Scored Under 4% on Mass Spectra. Antigravity Skills Put Lightweight Flash at 97%.
propus.standfirstHtml: Over 90% of chemical signals recorded in modern metabolomics remain unannotated because reference spectral libraries only cover a sliver of known molecules. On November 25, 2026, Google DeepMind unveiled Mass Spec Skills for Google Antigravity, pairing Gemini’s chemical reasoning with established open-source analytical tools so even lightweight Gemini 3.8 Flash matches frontier Gemini 4 models at around 97% identification accuracy while burning nearly 4x fewer tokens.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: On 100 Enamine REAL MS/MS spectra in MoNA, Antigravity without internet or skills scored under 4%, and internet-only custom scripts missed 25%–33% on frontier models and over 75% on Flash; adding Mass Spec Skills lifted Gemini 3.8 Flash, Gemini 4 Argon, and Gemini 4 Carbon all to around 97% exact-match accuracy.

Validated skills cut generated tokens per attempt nearly fourfold on Gemini 3.8 Flash, by half on Gemini 4 Argon, and nearly a fifth on Gemini 4 Carbon, while resolving tied 97.7%-intensity PubChem isomers (CID 137835447 vs. CID 55558151 and CID 154638626) via HCl and HNCO neutral losses.

LC-MS/MS spectra alone cannot distinguish mirror-image stereoisomers or near-identical isomers that fragment identically (requiring retention time, ion mobility, or NMR), and brand-new natural products absent from PubChem receive formula and substructure leads rather than confirmed database IDs.

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · SCIENTIFIC PRODUCTIVITY & MODEL ECONOMICS LENS
castor.titleHtml: Why Domain Skills Beat Raw Model Scaling in Specialized Science
castor.subtitleHtml: How packaging matchms, SIRIUS, MAGMa, MetFrag, and RDKit as structured Antigravity skills turns a lightweight fast-tier model into a 97%-accurate analytical chemist assistant.
paragraphsHtml: A single drop of blood, soil, or plant extract run through a modern tandem mass spectrometer produces tens of thousands of molecular signals. Yet even after a decade of community library growth, direct spectral lookup annotates roughly 5% of measured spectra on average—and only about 10% in human samples—leaving the vast majority as the so-called "dark matter" of mass spectrometry.

In From spectrum to structure: Identifying molecules with Mass Spec Skills for Google Antigravity (published November 25, 2026 by Robert Brunck, Stefan Ganscha, Swaroop Guntupalli, and Google DeepMind collaborators alongside chemists at the University of Pretoria, Technical University of Denmark, and Princeton University’s Rabinowitz Lab), DeepMind tackles the bottleneck directly. Instead of training a bespoke monolithic chemistry model, the team packaged community-standard analytical software—matchms, GNPS, MoNA, SIRIUS, MAGMa, MetFrag, PubChem, and RDKit—into composable Google Antigravity skills.

The benchmark result on 100 compounds sampled from the Enamine REAL MS/MS collection in MoNA carries a striking architectural lesson for every AI builder, not just chemists. Left with raw peak lists and no tools, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Gemini 4 Argon, and Gemini 4 Carbon all scored below 4%. Given internet access alone, models improvised brittle Python scrapers that tripped over precursor windows, adducts, and noise spikes—causing frontier models to miss a quarter to a third of spectra and Flash to miss more than three-quarters. Once DeepMind gave the exact same models curated Mass Spec Skills, all three converged at roughly 97% exact-match accuracy.

Just as important for R&D budgets and high-throughput labs studying thousands of spectra per run, structured skills sharply compress inference waste. Rather than burning context debugging one-off API calls, the agent invokes tested chemistry primitives and focuses its reasoning tokens on interpreting fragmentation evidence—cutting generated tokens nearly 4x on Gemini 3.8 Flash, by half on Gemini 4 Argon, and by nearly a fifth on Gemini 4 Carbon.

pullquote.quoteHtml: When domain software is packaged into deterministic skills, a lightweight model can match frontier retrieval accuracy at a fraction of the token cost—turning days of manual spectral detective work into an auditable report.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: Can Mass Spec Skills discover brand-new natural products that are not in PubChem?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: If a molecule is absent from every public chemical database, Antigravity cannot confirm an exact database ID automatically. However, it still automates preprocessing, library screening, elemental formula determination, and fragment-substructure mapping—giving analytical chemists an auditable starting point in hours rather than weeks.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: Why did Gemini 3.8 Flash jump from under 25% to ~97% parity with Gemini 4 Carbon once Skills were added?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: Ad-hoc tool scripting forces the model to handle exact floating-point tolerances, adduct math, and HTTP edge cases simultaneously. Moving that mechanical surface into deterministic SKILL.md tool wrappers lets lightweight Flash allocate its reasoning budget solely to tool orchestration and chemical tie-breaking.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: Which physical measurements still sit outside an LC-MS/MS skill workflow?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: Mirror-image molecules (enantiomers) and certain closely related positional isomers yield virtually identical MS/MS fragmentation patterns. Separating them still requires orthogonal lab evidence such as chromatographic retention time, ion mobility spectrometry, or NMR.

pollux.kickerHtml: PART II · β POLLUX · 6-STAGE ELUCIDATION PIPELINE & TIE-BREAK CHEMISTRY LENS
pollux.titleHtml: Inside the Worked Example: How Antigravity Resolved an 845-Isomer Tie at 97.7% Spectral Coverage
pollux.subtitleHtml: Walking peak-by-peak through matchms denoising, SIRIUS fragmentation trees, MAGMa/MetFrag scoring, HCl + HNCO neutral-loss loops, and RDKit bond-break penalties on m/z 395.1387.
paragraphsHtml: DeepMind’s worked example on a negative-mode tandem spectrum (precursor [M−H]− at m/z 395.1387, corresponding to a neutral molecular mass of 396.1459 Da) exposes exactly why naive spectral-coverage scoring fails. First, the agent invokes matchms with configurable intensity thresholds to strip out 1,742 low-intensity noise spikes, compressing 1,761 raw peaks down to 19 clean fragment signals. Next, cosine-similarity queries against GNPS and MoNA confirm no high-confidence library match, triggering de novo formula deduction.

Running SIRIUS fragmentation-tree scoring across ten candidate elements isolates the chlorinated formula C20H21ClN6O at −1.5 ppm mass error with a score of 37.86 (comfortably ahead of the 28.33 runner-up). Inside that tree, the molecule splits into two complementary halves whose formulas sum to the intact precursor: m/z 162.1037 ([C9H12N3]−, 45.1% intensity) and m/z 232.0283 ([C11H7ClN3O]−, 6.8% intensity). From m/z 232.0283, sequential neutral losses of hydrogen chloride (HCl) and isocyanic acid (HNCO) in both orders trace a closed loop via m/z 196.0511 and m/z 189.0238 down to m/z 153.0453—chemical proof of a chlorine atom and a central urea linkage on the same half.

When MAGMa and MetFrag score all 845 C20H21ClN6O isomers in PubChem, multiple distinct structures tie at the exact same 97.7% summed fragment intensity (matching 14 of 19 preprocessed peaks). Because mass-matching alone cannot break that tie, Gemini inspects bond connectivity: it rejects a fused triazolobenzazepinol isomer (CID 154638626) that lacks any urea group to lose HNCO and shows only baseline noise at expected water-loss masses (m/z 377.1281 and 214.0178), rejects an amide runner-up (CID 55558151) requiring higher-energy C−C cleavage and aromatic-ring breaks (MAGMa sum bond-break penalty 49.0), and confirms the five-regioisomer urea family down to CID 137835447 (bond-break score 26.0) via chlorophenyl-pyrazole fragments (m/z 206.0485, 126.0114) and RDKit valence verification.

builderRules.labelHtml: 01 · Wrap Brittle Mass Math & Adduct Windows Into Deterministic Skills
builderRules.detailHtml: Never ask an LLM to hand-roll adduct offsets or HTTP library queries from scratch; package matchms, SIRIUS, MAGMa, and RDKit behind typed skill contracts so even Gemini 3.8 Flash hits ~97% accuracy.

builderRules.labelHtml: 02 · Enforce Mechanistic Tie-Breaking Beyond Peak Coverage Percentages
builderRules.detailHtml: Two incompatible isomers can match the same 97.7% of summed fragment intensity; require agents to verify diagnostic neutral-loss loops (such as HCl + HNCO) and bond-break penalties before declaring a winner.

builderRules.labelHtml: 03 · Surface Complementary Physical Assays Whenever Fragmentation Ambiguity Remains
builderRules.detailHtml: Build explicit uncertainty branches in scientific agent reports flagging enantiomers or co-eluting isomers where retention time, ion mobility, or NMR is mandatory to confirm structure.

castor.titleHtml: Why Google Split AI Agents Off From 2.8 Trillion Monthly REST Calls
castor.subtitleHtml: How Google’s Workspace AI Tools Addendum, Admin Console approval rules, and Cloud Agent Gateway replace fragile DIY OAuth scripts with an auditable agent boundary.
paragraphsHtml: Workspace APIs now process more than 2.8 trillion calls every month across 4 billion users and 13 million organizations, with public Google Drive traffic alone running over two-and-a-half times higher than two years ago. Traditional SaaS integrations execute predictable code paths written by humans; autonomous AI agents compose multi-step read, summarize, share, and send chains at runtime inside live corporate mailboxes and document repositories.

In twin November 24, 2026 announcements across the Google Cloud Blog (Built for trust and control: Powering the next wave of AI agents across Google Workspace and Google Cloud) and Google Workspace Updates, Google established a unified control plane for that shift. Instead of scraping raw payloads line by line over REST APIs, agents now connect through Google-hosted Workspace Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers in the cloud or the native Google Workspace CLI (gwscli) inside local terminals, VMs, and containerized sandboxes.

For CIOs and security leaders, the core unlock is centralized visibility and revocation without blocking builders. Existing Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies apply automatically on every MCP and CLI request, external agents must declare the dedicated AI-agent OAuth client flag in Google Cloud console, administrators can enforce human-in-the-loop (HITL) approvals under Security > API Controls and Agents > Settings > User review for external agents, and the revised Workspace AI Tools Addendum forbids extended derived-data storage, model training, or API scraping.

For engineering founders and developer toolmakers, the most urgent operational takeaway is the migration clock. Starting February 1, 2027, technical enforcement requires AI agents to call Workspace MCP servers or gwscli rather than direct Workspace REST APIs—any agent still hitting REST directly gets capped at Standard Tier quotas regardless of billing configuration. Two months later, on April 1, 2027, Scaled Tier billing goes live across Gmail, Calendar, and Drive.

pollux.kickerHtml: PART II · β POLLUX · STATELESS FORM ELICITATION, GWSCLI & GATEWAY ARCHITECTURE LENS
pollux.titleHtml: Inside /mcp/v1 Elicitation, Argument-Locked requestState & Dynamic gwscli Discovery
pollux.subtitleHtml: Dissecting the 2026-07-28 stateless MCP approval protocol, /mcp/v1self fallback routing, gwscli binary workflows, and SPIFFE Agent Gateway wiring.
paragraphsHtml: At the protocol layer, Google’s GA servers expose dedicated endpoints for Gmail (gmailmcp.googleapis.com), Drive (drivemcp.googleapis.com), Docs (docsmcp.googleapis.com), Sheets (sheetsmcp.googleapis.com), Slides (slidesmcp.googleapis.com), Calendar (calendarmcp.googleapis.com), Chat (chatmcp.googleapis.com), Tasks (tasksmcp.googleapis.com), Classroom (classroommcp.googleapis.com), and cross-app Universal Search (workspacemcp.googleapis.com), alongside People MCP on people.googleapis.com in Developer Preview. Each server pairs a primary /mcp/v1 route with a limited /mcp/v1self fallback for legacy MCP hosts that cannot render forms yet.

Because server-side governance changes dynamically across user preferences and organizational units, clients must never hardcode which tools need confirmation or cache approvals locally. On /mcp/v1, an MCP host advertises elicitation support in params._meta. When a sensitive call such as create_event with external attendees or send_message hits a policy gate, the server pauses and returns resultType: "input_required" containing an elicitation/create payload (mode: "form") under inputRequests["approval_choice"] plus an opaque requestState string cryptographically bound to the exact tool arguments. Once the user picks ALLOW_ONCE or DENY_ONCE, the host replays the exact same tool call with params.requestState and params.inputResponses to complete execution—and prebuilt hosts like Google Antigravity or Claude Desktop should set local host confirmations to Always allow on /mcp/v1 so users never suffer double prompts.

For terminal-native coding agents such as Google Antigravity, Claude Code, and Codex running inside dev laptops, VMs, or remote containers, gwscli eliminates boilerplate SDK wrappers. Installed as a standalone binary from dl.google.com/workspace-cli/, it authenticates via incremental OAuth (for example gwscli auth login --bundle readonly or scoped "chat search_messages"), exposes --show-scopes and --print-scope-only for headless bearer tokens, and lets agents inspect live commands and JSON schemas via --help and --schema. Inside Google Cloud production fleets, Cloud Agent Gateway complements those Workspace controls with SPIFFE IDs in Agent Registry, mTLS + DPoP authentication, default-deny IAM Unified Access Policies, inline Model Armor prompt-injection scanning, and Semantic Governance Policies.
